rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disjoint letters occur beyond the Ḥā Mīm sūras and usually lead into discussion of the Qur'an; the best known view is that Arabs are challenged to match revelation made from their own speech elements.
rows.anchor: وأشهر ما قيل في ذلك أن هذا الكتاب الذي تحداكم به وأنزله رب العالمين هو من مفردات كلامكم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another reported view is that the disjoint letters are combined to form words.
rows.anchor: وقسم قال أنه يجمع بين الأحرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is about the first-person yāʾ, not only forms such as ليَ and لي; its vowel may be open or unvowelled where language and transmitted Qur'anic readings permit.
rows.anchor: هذه مسألة ياء المتكلم فتح ياء المتكلم وعدم فتحها ولا تتعلق فقط بـ (ليَ ولي)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first-person yāʾ must be opened after a maqṣūr noun, an inflected noun ending in a necessary alif; this explains عصايَ, هدايَ and محيايَ.
rows.anchor: والاسم المقصور هو الإسم المُعرَب الذي آخره ألف لازمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order placing a nation's not preceding its term before its not being delayed occurs only in contexts of destruction and punishment; al-Aʿrāf reverses the order.
rows.anchor: تقديم (ما تسبق من أمة أجلها) على (وما يستأخرون) لم تأت إلا في مقام الإهلاك والعقوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baqara puts disclosure first because it speaks of reckoning for deeds; Āl ʿImrān puts concealment first because it speaks of God's knowledge, who knows the secret and what is more hidden.
rows.anchor: في سياق المحاسبة قدّم الإبداء أما في سورة آل عمران فالآية في سياق العلم لذا قدّم الإخفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without wāw, صم بكم can mean that some are deaf and some mute, or that all are both; with wāw, صم وبكم means that all are both.
rows.anchor: صم بكم يحتمل أن يكون بعضهم صم وبعضهم بكم ويحتمل أن يكونوا في مجموعهم صم بكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Anʿām omits عمي, while al-Baqara includes it in its longer discussion of hypocrites and their conduct, such as mockery.
rows.anchor: في سورة الأنعام لم يقل "عمي" وإنما قال (صم وبكم) فقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blindness is more severe than being in darkness: a blind person cannot see whether surrounded by darkness or light.
rows.anchor: الأعمى أشد من الذي في الظلام لأن الأعمى سواء كان في الظلمات أو في النور فهو لا يرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although deafness is commonly associated with muteness, not every deaf person is unable to speak; there are types of deafness, and some deaf people speak.
rows.anchor: المعروف أن الأصم هو أبكم لكن ليس كل أصم لا يتكلم فهناك أنواع من الصمم؛ قسم من الصم يتكلم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say al-Anʿām 6:39 describes the afterlife; the speaker in Ṭā Hā 20:125 is blind yet can speak and hear.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم أن آية سورة الأنعام هي في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated comparison says disclosure precedes concealment in al-Baqara's reckoning context, whereas concealment precedes disclosure in Āl ʿImrān's knowledge context.
rows.anchor: المحاسبة في سورة البقرة هي على ما يُبدي الإنسان وليس ما يُخفي ففي سياق المحاسبة قدّم الإبداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath response تالله تفتأ omits لا but means لا تفتأ; the author calls it the Qur'an's only case of an omitted negative particle in an oath response and gives a rule contrasting والله أفعل with والله لأفعل.
rows.anchor: هذا هو الموطن الوحيد في القرآن الذي حُذف فيه حرف النفي جواباً للقسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Omitting لا is less emphatic, fitting the brothers' uncertain claim that Jacob would keep remembering Joseph until death; that outcome did not occur, unlike the certain assertions in other Qur'anic oaths.
rows.anchor: الذكر يفيد التوكيد والحذف أقل توكيداً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فتأ can mean forget, quiet or calm, and extinguish a fire; the verb gathers the senses of time easing loss, quieting separation's ache, and extinguishing grief's flame.
rows.anchor: فتأ: من معانيها في اللغة نسي وسكّن وأطفأ النار يقال فتأت النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though تفتأ, like ما زال and ما برح, signals continued action, it is chosen over لا أبرح because its senses of calming, forgetting and extinguishing a fire all suit Jacob's continuing grief.
rows.anchor: فهي تختلف بدلالة خاصة فهي تأتي بمعنى سكّن وبمعنى نسي وبمعنى أطفأ النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's grief neither cools nor fades from memory nor stops being spoken of; the omitted negative particle also leaves the brothers' oath less certain.
rows.anchor: إضافة إلى ذلك حذف حرف النفي الذي لا يدل على التوكيد فالكلام في الآية غير متيقن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baqara 2:274 adds fāʾ because giving by night and day, secretly and openly, is detailed and signals sincerity, calling for emphasis; 2:262 mentions giving generally and omits it.
rows.anchor: في مقام التوكيد والتفصيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb combines continued remembrance with its other senses: a bereaved person may calm with time, forget, or have grief's inner fire extinguished, but Jacob does none of these.
rows.anchor: إذن كلمة (فتأ) لها ثلاثة معاني سكّن وأطفأ النار ونسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's grief remains intense rather than calming, forgetting or going out; the Qur'an's report that his eyes whitened from sorrow and he was choked with grief supports this reading.
rows.anchor: أراد أن يعقوب لا ينسى ولا يكفّ بدليل قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an uses تفتأ only here, while it uses forms such as يزال and يوال elsewhere; this unique choice carries the senses needed in Jacob's case.
rows.anchor: والقرآن الكريم لم يستعمل هذه الكلمة إلا في هذا الموضع في سورة يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the expected form is لا تفتأ; a negative or quasi-negative use can convey negation even without لا, as in the poetic oath and والله أذهب.
rows.anchor: إذا لم تأتي بـ (لا) فهو نفي قطعاً كقول الشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order Ibrahim, Isaac, Jacob groups father and descendants: Isaac is Ibrahim's son and Jacob is Isaac's son.
rows.anchor: إبراهيم وإسحق ويعقوب، واسحق ابن إبراهيم ويعقوب ابن اسحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David and Solomon are paired through both sonship and kingship.
rows.anchor: داوود وسليمان (العلاقة بينهم البنوّة والمُلك)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Job and Joseph share God's bestowal after prophethood and trial.
rows.anchor: أيوب ويوسف (العلاقة بينهما أنهما يشتركان في الإنعام بعد النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon and Job are both called excellent servants who turn to God; Solomon is grateful and Job patient, and gratitude and patience together comprise faith.
rows.anchor: فأيوب هو العبد الصابر وسليمان هو العبد الشاكر، والصبر والشُكر جماع الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses and Aaron are paired as brothers.
rows.anchor: موسى وهارون (العلاقة بينهما هي الأخوّة)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zechariah and John are paired through their father-son relationship.
rows.anchor: زكريا ويحيى (علاقة البنوّة)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: John and Jesus have unusual births: John was born to an elderly father and a barren mother, while Jesus was born to a mother without a father; both are presented together in Āl ʿImrān and Maryam.
rows.anchor: كلاهما مُستغرب الولادة فيحيى جاء من أبوين أحدهما شيخ والآخر عقيم وعيسى جاء من أم بلا أب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus closes the first lineage sequence because he has no father.
rows.anchor: ختم تعالى هذه المجموعة بعيسى - عليه السلام - لأنه ليس له أب فكان خاتمة النسب الأول عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next group follows another descent: Elias is not from Isaac's line, Ishmael is Isaac's brother, and Elisha is Elias's companion and is paired with him in mention.
rows.anchor: إلياس ليس من ذرية اسحق، إسماعيل أخو إسحق، اليسع صاحب إلياس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah and Lot are not descendants of Abraham; both left their people as migrants, and the Qur'an pairs them in al-Ṣāffāt, where Jonah leaves angry and Lot says he is migrating to his Lord.
rows.anchor: ويونس ليس من ذرية إبراهيم وكذلك لوط ليس من ذرية إبراهيم، ويونس ولوط كلاهما مهاجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ordered list begins with Abraham going to his Lord and ends with Lot migrating to his Lord, suggesting divine wisdom in the arrangement as well as its structure.
rows.anchor: بدأ بالذاهب إلى ربه أي إبراهيم - عليه السلام -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic word order can express distinct information about who gave, what was given and to whom; its many grammatical permutations capture distinctions that may be expressed by a single sentence in another language.
rows.anchor: أحياناً عندنا 25 جملة في العربية أو أكثر كل واحدة لها معنى يقابلها جملة واحدة في اللغات الأخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 22:28 and 22:34, general remembrance of God is followed by the specific bahīmat al-anʿām; 22:30 discusses livestock itself, so it simply names al-anʿām. The author calls this a linguistic congruity of general followed by specific.
rows.anchor: خاص بعد عامّ وبهمية الأنعام خاص بعد عامّ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Qur'anic usage, سنة usually suggests drought and hardship, as in Arabic expressions for a barren year, while عام usually carries a positive sense.
rows.anchor: كلمة (سنة) في القرآن تدلّ عادة على الجدب والقحط

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Exegetes say Noah spent 950 years preaching amid hardship, denial and mockery, then fifty years after the flood with believers in calm and ease.
rows.anchor: يقول المفسرون: أنه لبث في الدعوة 950 سنة مع قومه بشدة وصعوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spelling of Ibrahim without yāʾ in al-Baqara, unlike elsewhere in the Qur'an, reflects the scribes' orthography and carries no basis for analogy or a separate meaning.
rows.anchor: إبراهيم في القرآن الكريم وردت منقوطة بالياء في كل القرآن إلا في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mushaf spelling varied with historical writing conventions and sometimes accommodates multiple transmitted readings, as ملك and مالك in al-Fātiḥa; a valid reading must agree with the rasm.
rows.anchor: أحياناً يكون الرسم لاختلاف القراءات فيوضع الرسم الذي يجمع القراءات المتواترة كما في سورة الفاتحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خلف is originally spatial, meaning behind; the author illustrates the sense with verses about Satan approaching from behind, a barrier behind people, God's knowledge of what is behind them and descendants left behind.
rows.anchor: أما خلف فهي في الأصل للمكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the verse about Pharaoh's body, those behind him are his people waiting for his return; the sign originally challenged them and later became a sign for everyone.
rows.anchor: من هم خلفه؟ هم قومه الذين ينتظرون عودة فرعون وماذا سيفعل فهم خلفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those described as not yet having joined the martyrs from behind them are people following them in battle; خلف retains its spatial sense.
rows.anchor: الذين معهم في المعركة والقتال فهي في الأصل خلف في المكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second al-Baqara verse includes fāʾ because its detailed giving by night and day, secretly and openly, adds emphasis and signals sincerity; the first gives no such detail and omits fāʾ.
rows.anchor: أما الآية الأولى فذكر فيها الإنفاق في سبيل الله ولم يفصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses ما for all creation because, in the Hereafter, humans have no choice or will and stand like inanimate things, plants and animals as objects under command.
rows.anchor: لأن كل المخلوقات تساوت عند الله ولا اختيار للناس في الآخرة كما كان لهم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ant chooses مساكنكم rather than houses or holes because the ants are moving and need to settle; the plural also suggests each ant has its own known dwelling.
rows.anchor: اختارت لفظ المساكن من السكون حتى يسكنوا فيها ولم تقل المساكن والجحور وإنما قالت (مساكنكم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She addresses the ants as rational beings, uses the masculine plural ادخلوا, and calls يا أيها النمل as a distant-address form so they will hear her.
rows.anchor: ثم أكدّت بالنداء بقولها (يا أيها النمل ادخلوا مساكنكم) حرف النداء الدال على البعد حتى يسمعوا نداءها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming Solomon alongside his troops, rather than saying Solomon's troops, removes an excuse for Solomon's lack of awareness of their action.
rows.anchor: وقالت (سليمان وجنوده) ولم تقل "جنود سليمان" حتى ترفع العذر عن سليمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She calls him simply Solomon, without a title such as prophet, because he is already famous without description.
rows.anchor: وجاءت بلفظ (سليمان) بدون أي لقب له كالنبي سليمان للدلالة على أنه مشهور بدون أن يوصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ant presses her people to act quickly before calamity reaches them.
rows.anchor: ثم حثتهم على الإسراع في التنفيذ قبل أن تنالهم المصيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ant attributes the crushing to Solomon and selects يحطمنكم as apt for smashing and severity; the author also claims ant bodies consist mostly of silicon, a material used in glass.
rows.anchor: وفعل يحطمنكم مقصود في الآية لأنه ثبت علمياً أن جسم النمل يتركب معظمه من كمية كبيرة من السليكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The key is not merely listing rhetorical features but showing how the particular expression conveys them; this is a distinctive feature of the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: لكن المهم كيف التعبير عن هذه الأوجه وهذا ما يتفرّد به القرآن الكريم
